issue_title: Performance regression: LCP spiked site-wide, all pages now below 85
issue_body:
## Performance Regression — 2026-08-31

All five audited pages regressed meaningfully on the 2026-08-31 nightly run. Every performance score fell below 85 and LCP worsened substantially on every page.

### Score changes

| Page | Prev | Now | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | 81 | 76 | −5 |
| `/about` | 90 | 83 | **−7** |
| `/projects` | 89 | 81 | **−8** |
| `/projects/note-structurer` | 80 | 71 | **−9** |
| `/projects/screenshot-to-primevue` | 76 | 69 | **−7** |

### LCP changes

| Page | Prev LCP | Now LCP | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | 4077 ms | 4315 ms | +238 ms |
| `/about` | 3300 ms | 4065 ms | **+765 ms** |
| `/projects` | 3304 ms | 4087 ms | **+784 ms** |
| `/projects/note-structurer` | 4316 ms | 5678 ms | **+1362 ms** |
| `/projects/screenshot-to-primevue` | 4817 ms | 6095 ms | **+1278 ms** |

### Likely cause
LCP inflated consistently across all pages in a single run, suggesting either a CDN/hosting cold-start, an unoptimised hero or LCP image element, or a recently introduced render-blocking resource.

### Recommended fix
1. Identify the LCP element on each page (typically the hero image or above-the-fold heading) and serve it as WebP at display dimensions with `fetchpriority="high"` and a `<link rel="preload">` in `<head>`.
2. Audit for any newly added render-blocking scripts or stylesheets and defer/async them.
3. Check CDN cache-hit rates — a global cache miss would explain the simultaneous spike across all pages.

### Visuals
No visual breakage was observed on any page (desktop or mobile). Accessibility, best-practices, and SEO remain perfect at 100 across the board.
